title: /mcp is exempt from the web auth layer; enabling HATCHDOOR_WEB_BEARER_TOKEN does not protect MCP read tools
affected: HATCHDOOR_MCP_ENABLED=true with no HATCHDOOR_MCP_BEARER_TOKEN and write disabled (read-only)
operator has set HATCHDOOR_WEB_BEARER_TOKEN believing the whole vault is locked down
non-browser client (curl) sending no Origin header, bypassing the origin allowlist
description: In build_router the /mcp route is attached to the OPEN router (line 86), deliberately outside the require_web_token layer that guards every /api route (lines 46-82). Authentication for /mcp is a fully independent system in validate_mcp_request (src/mcp/config.rs:108-166): the MCP bearer token is only enforced when config.bearer_token is Some, and a read-only MCP deployment (write_enabled=false) is valid with bearer_token=None (validate() only requires a token for write mode). The origin allowlist is skipped when no Origin header is present (config.rs:131), so a headless client is unaffected. Net effect: POST /mcp tools/call can invoke search_notes / get_note / get_tree and read the entire vault with no credentials, even though HATCHDOOR_WEB_BEARER_TOKEN is set.
why: The two token systems are independent and the coupling gap is non-obvious. An operator who locks down the web UI for a public launch and turns on MCP for their own assistant, without also setting the MCP token, silently exposes full vault contents. MCP is off by default, which bounds the blast radius, but it is a real data-exposure path.
fixSketch: Require an MCP bearer token whenever MCP is enabled (make validate() reject enabled && bearer_token.is_none(), not just write mode), or make /mcp inherit the web token when set; at minimum log a loud startup warning when MCP is enabled tokenless.

verdicts.reason: main.rs:84-87 confirms /mcp route (mcp_get_handler/mcp_post_handler) is attached to the outer Router before .merge(protected), so it sits outside the require_web_token layer applied only to the protected router (lines 76-82). The mechanism as described is real in this source.

title: Attachment uploads are capped at axum's 2 MB default body limit while 10 MB is advertised/enforced downstream
affected: POST /api/attachment (upload_attachment_handler) with a file between 2 MB and max_attachment_bytes (default 10 MB)
any deployment relying on advertised HATCHDOOR_MCP_MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES (default 10*1024*1024)
description: build_router (src/main.rs:43-109) never sets DefaultBodyLimit, so axum 0.8's 2 MB default request-body limit applies to every extractor including the Multipart extractor used by upload_attachment_handler. The handler passes state.mcp_config.max_attachment_bytes (default 10*1024*1024, src/mcp/config.rs:82) into import_attachment_bytes (write_api.rs:186) as the real ceiling, and that same 10 MB value is advertised to clients via MCP tools output (src/mcp/tools.rs:52,396). A 3-10 MB image is rejected by the framework with a generic 413 before handler code runs, so the 10 MB limit is unreachable over HTTP and the advertised value is misleading.
why: Users are told 10 MB is allowed but real uploads fail at 2 MB with an opaque framework error (no ErrorResponse JSON body), reading as a broken upload feature. Exactly the advertised-vs-actual body-size mismatch flagged for launch.
fixSketch: Apply an explicit DefaultBodyLimit sized from max_attachment_bytes (plus multipart overhead) to the attachment route and keep JSON routes at a sane limit; ensure advertised max matches the enforced framework limit.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed no DefaultBodyLimit layer/extractor override anywhere in src (grep found none), so axum's default 2MB body limit applies to the Multipart extractor used at write_api.rs:112/186, while max_attachment_bytes (10MB default) is passed into import_attachment_bytes as an application-level ceiling that is unreachable for bodies between 2MB and 10MB. Mechanism is real.

title: Bearer token accepted as an access_token query parameter, exposing it in URLs and (at debug log level) request spans
affected: tower_http log level raised to debug, where DefaultMakeSpan records the full request URI
reverse proxies / browser history / Referer headers that capture full URLs
description: request_is_authorized accepts the web token via the access_token query parameter (auth.rs:54-58) to support /download navigations that cannot set an Authorization header. The TraceLayer DefaultMakeSpan (src/main.rs:104-106) records the request URI including the query string, so raising tower_http to debug writes the token to logs. The default filter (tower_http=info, src/app_state.rs:109) suppresses that span so it is not leaked by default, but the token still lands in browser history, proxy access logs, and potentially Referer headers for the affected URLs.
why: Secrets in URLs are a recognized weakness; even with the default log level, the long-lived token is durably exposed in intermediaries the app does not control. Relevant to hardening before a public launch.
fixSketch: Use a short-lived, scoped signed token (or a cookie derived from the Authorization header) for asset/download URLs instead of the long-lived web bearer token, and redact the query string in the trace span.

verdicts.reason: auth.rs:54-58 confirms access_token is accepted from the query string in request_is_authorized, and main.rs:104-106 shows TraceLayer with DefaultMakeSpan (include_headers(false) only suppresses headers, not the URI/query recorded by DefaultMakeSpan). The mechanism matches the claim.

title: When HATCHDOOR_WEB_BEARER_TOKEN is unset, all mutating routes are fully unauthenticated with only an info-level guardrail
affected: HOST=0.0.0.0 (or fronted without an auth proxy) exposing the port beyond localhost
description: build_router only wraps the protected router in the auth layer when web_bearer_token is Some (main.rs:76-82); when None the entire router - including POST /api/note, PUT/DELETE /api/note/{slug}, the rename/move/archive PATCH routes, and POST /api/attachment - is served unauthenticated. The only guardrail against public exposure is an info-level startup log (main.rs:122-127) when host==0.0.0.0 with no token, plus a warning string in the /api/write-capabilities body (write_api.rs:92-99). Nothing refuses to start or downgrades to read-only. Default host is 127.0.0.1 which bounds risk, but HOST=0.0.0.0 with a forgotten token silently exposes anonymous create/delete of the vault.
why: For a public launch, an insecure-by-default allowing anonymous overwrite/deletion of the vault, guarded only by an easily-missed info log, is a foot-gun. Content-hash checks stop blind overwrites but not create/upload or hash-then-delete sequences.
fixSketch: Refuse to bind a non-loopback host without a web token (hard error), or auto-disable frontend write routes when no token is configured, instead of only logging at info level.

verdicts.reason: main.rs:76-82 confirms the auth layer is applied only when web_bearer_token is Some; when None the protected router (with all mutating routes) merges unwrapped at line 87. main.rs:122-127 shows only an info-level log as guardrail, no refusal to start or read-only downgrade. Mechanism is accurately described.
